request: Should we keep the AI review pass on our pull requests after the pilot?
facts: For a six-week pilot, an AI review pass ran on every pull request of our eight-person team, to shorten the time humans spend reviewing. The pilot ends on Friday and the pass switches off unless we sign up; it can be switched off again at any time, and nothing in the code depends on it.
Median human review time per pull request was 26 minutes during the pilot (120 pull requests, measured by the review tool), against 39 minutes in the six weeks before.
Of the 210 points the pass raised, authors accepted 172 as real problems. The team already used a linter and a formatter before the pilot, so the time saved came on top of them.
It costs $2,400 a month, more than all of the team's other tools together.
Keeping its noise down takes about half a day a week of rule tuning, which comes out of one engineer's feature work.
In an anonymous survey, seven of the eight engineers want to keep it and the eighth has no preference. Reviewers say they now spend review time on design questions instead of style and typos.
note: Designed conflict, expected 2-1 passed: each fact speaks to one unit's question. MELCHIOR-1 (does the means reach the goal): facts 2 and 3, review time down by a third with accepted findings on top of the existing linter, so approve. BALTHASAR-2 (what it costs to carry): facts 4 and 5, money and an engineer's time every week, so reject. CASPER-3 (is it wanted, what is gained): fact 6, so approve. Fact 1 is context and makes the decision reversible, so the grade should be normal. The request says 'keep', not 'require', so no optional variant is suggested by the wording, and no cause or cheaper alternative is named. First version (goal missed, mostly noise, 'require on every pull request'): rejected 0/3 in all three 1.5.1 runs; every unit pointed to an optional pass.
